mcat_description.short: PUF Cabin is a prefabricated, portable insulated structure built using polyurethane foam (PUF) sandwich panels as walls and roof, sold as a complete assembled or knock-down unit. It is used as a site office, security cabin, labour accommodation, or temporary housing and is available in custom dimensions.
mcat_description.long: A PUF Cabin is a modular, relocatable building constructed from PUF (Polyurethane Foam) insulated sandwich panels — a rigid closed-cell foam core bonded between two pre-painted galvanised steel (PPGI) or FRP skins — mounted on a mild steel structural frame. The panels provide superior thermal insulation (thermal conductivity ≤ 0.024 W/mK), weather resistance, and lightweight portability, making these cabins a fast-deploy alternative to conventional brick-and-mortar construction. In the Indian B2B market, PUF cabins are manufactured and supplied as complete turnkey units or in knock-down form for on-site assembly, with standard panel thicknesses ranging from 30 mm to 150 mm and cabin dimensions fully customisable to buyer requirements. Key end-use sectors include construction project sites, oil and gas installations, defence and government facilities, industrial plants, and residential farm-house applications.

market_context: PUF Cabins in India are prefabricated portable structures built from polyurethane foam sandwich panels (PUF/PUR core, PPGI or FRP skins) on mild steel frames, serving as a fast-deploy, thermally insulated alternative to conventional construction. The Indian market is dominated by manufacturers in Delhi-NCR, Haryana, Maharashtra, Gujarat, and Punjab, supplying to construction, infrastructure, oil and gas, defence, and industrial sectors. Panel specifications follow industry norms of 40 kg/m³ core density, thermal conductivity ≤ 0.024 W/mK, and panel thickness ranging from 30 mm to 150 mm; PPGI sheet conforming to IS 12436:1988 is the standard skin material. Leading Indian manufacturers include EPACK Prefab (GRIHA certified, BMTPC PAC No. 1060-S/2022), Kingspan Jindal (PIR/PUR panels), and numerous regional fabricators. Cabins are sold as complete turnkey units or in knock-down panel form, with dimensions fully customisable; common standard sizes include 10×10 ft, 10×20 ft, and 20×20 ft. The market distinguishes between small security/guard cabins (sold per piece), mid-size office cabins (quoted per sq ft), and large multi-room accommodation structures (quoted per project). PIR (Polyisocyanurate) panels are an advanced variant offering better fire resistance and lower K-value, used where fire safety compliance is critical.
